summary: Cab built 1940 to a Region 5 plan; tower in service in 1991 when moved to the Bieber museum grounds, but only the cab was reassembled there.

facts.design: Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin on an enclosed timber tower (NHLR)
facts.status_note: Only the cab was reassembled at the Big Valley Museum; the tower itself was not reassembled there

staffing.status: in operation as a fire lookout in March 1991; no later staffing reported

facts.agency: Big Valley Historical Museum, Bieber, California (current custodian of the cab)

events.note: California District News Letter item of July 13, 1923 (quoted by Forest Lookouts) mentions a visit to the new lookout house on Hayden Hill; not reconciled with the 1940 build date
Cab built to Region 5 Plan BC-301, per the register
Forest Lookouts quotes a 1943 item mentioning the Lookout Station on Hayden Hill
Supervisors approved moving the tower to the Bieber Museum grounds in March 1991; the actual move date is not in the sources, and only the cab was reassembled

evidence.supports: built in 1940 as a Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin on a 10 foot enclosed timber tower
evidence.quote: Hayden Hill Lookout was constructed in 1940 and is described as a California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin on a 10 foot enclosed timber tower in both of Thornton's surveys.

evidence.supports: site withdrawn for administrative use in 1912; structure stood by 1915
evidence.quote: The site was withdrawn for Administrative use in 1912 and structure stood by 1915.
1912: Site was approved for administrative use.

evidence.supports: July 1923 California District News Letter item about a visit to the new lookout house on Hayden Hill
evidence.quote: The next day Susanville was reached via Adin and a visit paid to the new lookout house on Hayden Hill.

evidence.supports: 1943 item places a man's wife caring for him at the Lookout Station
evidence.quote: His wife is taking care of him at the Lookout Station at Hayden Hill.
During the period of 1942 through 1946 this lookout made 13 first discoveries.

evidence.supports: March 1991 supervisors approved relocating the tower to the Bieber Museum grounds
evidence.quote: The supervisors last week approved a request from museum board member Carl Parks to relocate the Hayden Hill fire lookout tower from its present site to the Bieber Museum grounds.

evidence.supports: tower was declared a historical site and remained in operation in 1991
evidence.quote: The 2-story tower has been declared a historical site, according to Parks, even while it remains in operation.

evidence.supports: a new tower had to be built first to avoid a lapse in coverage
evidence.quote: a new tower must be built and made operational, since there cannot by law be a lapse in coverage of the area

evidence.supports: Amax Gold to handle dismantling, relocating and reassembly
evidence.quote: Amax Gold, whose Lassen Gold Mining subsidiary is currently in the midst of developing the Hayden Hill area, will take care of the actual dismantling, relocating, and reassembling of the tower

evidence.supports: only the cab was reassembled at the museum and stands today
evidence.quote: The cabin, but not the tower has been reassembled at the Museum and stands today.

evidence.supports: location on the Big Valley Museum grounds in Bieber
evidence.quote: Big Valley Museum Grounds - Bieber, California

evidence.supports: as of 1991 one of the best examples of an L-101 tower with BC-301 cab still in California
evidence.quote: As of 1991, this lookout was one of the best examples of an L-101 tower with BC-301 cab still in existence in California.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1940 for the cab. Forest Lookouts quotes a 1923 new lookout house on the same hill. Both are reported; the story does not pick one and says the relation is unclear.
The record's relocation note says the lookout moved. The register says only the cab was reassembled at the museum. The story follows the register.

notes_for_editor: Only two sources were read. Access is not stated, and the allowed access levels do not include unknown, so no access key was written; the story says to check with the museum. The Big Valley Historical Museum Facebook page returned no text, and the tipurdy Hayden Hill history page has no lookout content. An academia.edu figure from a search (not read) says the 1940 cab went to the Big Valley Historical Museum; read it if a third source is wanted. The 1923 house and the 1940 cab are unreconciled, and the move date is not recorded anywhere read. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the 1923 item is a California District News Letter item, not a newspaper; the status_note was changed to say the tower was not reassembled at the museum (the register does not say it was moved), and the corrections entry that proposed that wording was applied and cleared.
